title: [Proposal]: native HTML walkthroughs with synchronized video export
body:
### What practical problem are you trying to solve?

A native Archify diagram already contains nodes, relationships, boundaries, legends and source evidence. When an author wants to explain it as a presentation or video, those facts should be reusable instead of asking an AI to rebuild the page, camera, soundtrack and export code for each diagram. The author still supplies the explanation and chooses what to emphasize.

### Why are the current capabilities insufficient?

Live/Still, focus and motion recording help readers inspect a diagram, but do not provide an authored sequence of scenes with explanations, local relationship drawings, captions and synchronized cues. A separate presentation also loses the original Viewer's notes, themes, presets and export entry point.

### What outcome would improve this?

Add an opt-in walkthrough attachment for existing native Archify HTML:

- `story scan / draft / attach` exposes source identities, creates an editable JSON brief and attaches its playback runtime. An AI writes source IDs and explanation text rather than presentation code.
- Reuse the original SVG, native motion and source evidence across the ten diagram families. Preserve the input document, topology, notes, Live/Still behavior and existing exports.
- Add Story to the native motion control, with a draggable playback timeline. Theme and preset changes propagate automatically.
- Add Story video to the existing Export menu, defaulting to 1920×1080 at 60 fps with synchronized audio. Reuse the same brief for playback and export.
- Keep interactive reduced-motion preferences intact. Export motion overrides remain in a separate render iframe; publication errors report whether the output was committed and where recovery files remain.

This scope adds playback and explanation authoring, without changing diagram layout or the typed input schemas. It does not infer business meaning, synthesize speech or support arbitrary third-party HTML as native Story input. Video encoding depends on browser WebCodecs support; bounded audio/video buffering remains part of the implementation.

### Related issues or PRs

Implementation: #1036. This proposal is being opened after implementation, following the [maintainer's request](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify/pull/1036#issuecomment-6309015384), to record the intended scope for agreement before merge.


### Safe to share

- [x] I removed secrets, private source, and personal or customer data.
